thread:
Tara: @olivia escalating — customer reports that after today's rollout responses are truncating mid-instruction when conversation context exceeds ~6k tokens. They say the bot drops instructions and starts repeating earlier context. They opened a ticket, gave an example convo.

Olivia: thanks — can you paste the example + request_id and model name? ask if they can share a stripped repro (no PII). I told them we'll prioritize. :eyes:

Tara: customer example (redacted):
```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v4","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role":"user","content":"<very long conversation... ~7.5k tokens>"}, {"role":"user","content":"Now, please do task: summarize the TODOs and list 1-5 concrete action items."}], "max_tokens":512 }'\n```
Customer provided request_id: req_20260612_0aa7b3 and timestamp. They said previously on rwd-large-v3 this worked fine, only after today's rollout to v4 it regresses.

Liam: thanks. quick checks — can you confirm: 1) are they using streaming? 2) any custom stop sequences? 3) region? 4) auth scope (org-level token)

Tara: streaming=false, no custom stops, region=us-west-2, token is org-scoped. They included raw response: it stops mid-sentence and repeats a prior sentence fragment, then returns "...". No 5xxs from their side.

sre-bot: alert: inference_latency_p95 for model rwd-large-v4 in us-west-2 increased +28% between 2026-06-12T03:10Z and 2026-06-12T03:20Z. No service 5xx spike.

deploy-bot: canary rollout rwd-large-v4 -> 40% traffic at 2026-06-12T03:08Z (deploy id dpl_8791).

Jordyn: tagging in — this smells like a KV-cache / attention-index mismatch. We saw a change in the new long-kernel when integrating packed-QKV optimization. If the kernel's cache pointer math is off by one for sequences > block_size, you can get silent drops and repeats. The bench-suite didn't trigger with our default test lengths (max was 6k), customer hit ~7.5k.

Liam: ok that's a good hypothesis. can you run a sanity script against v4? repro steps:
```python
# minimal repro (python)
import requests
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer [REDACTED]', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Redwood-Force-Kernel': 'long-new'}
messages = [{'role':'system','content':'You are a helpful assistant.'}]
# append long filler to push >7000 tokens
messages.append({'role':'user', 'content': ' '.join(['foo']*4000)})
messages.append({'role':'user', 'content': 'Please summarize the action items from the above conversation and list them.'})
resp = requests.post(url, json={'model':'rwd-large-v4','messages':messages,'max_tokens':512}, headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```
Run same against rwd-large-v3 and compare outputs. Also try header X-Redwood-Force-Kernel: legacy to force old kernel.

Tara: running now against customer example + our minimal script, will paste outputs.

(30s later)

Tara: repro confirmed — against v4 output truncates and then repeats a prior clause; against v3 it completes the instruction. I captured response bodies and request ids: req_20260612_0aa7b3 (customer), local repro req_local_179955.

Jordyn: ok we should rollback canary to v3 for now. I'll open a bug with priority P0 and attach kernel traces. Suspect fix is to revert the pointer math change in the packed-QKV path, add long-seq unit tests (8k+), and validate KV indexing.

Liam: agreed. ops — can we gate rollback for only rwd-large-v4 traffic in us-west-2 where latency spike is? We don't want global rollback yet. Olivia, can you ask customer if they'd like immediate rollback for their org?

Olivia: asked customer — they replied yes, please rollback traffic for their org. gave greenlight to proceed.

deploy-bot: rollback started for dpl_8791 in us-west-2 at 2026-06-12T03:42Z. rolling to rwd-large-v3 for affected orgs.

sre-bot: note: after rollback p95 latency returned to baseline within 3m. No increase in error rates during rollback.

Jordyn: I'll prepare a patch branch and add tests hitting 9k and 12k contexts. Will also run differential output checks between kernels to catch repeat patterns.

Liam: Alyo (ops) — can you push a hotfix canary after tests? we want to validate fix in a staging cluster with longer sequences before re-rollout.

Tara: thanks team. I'll update the customer's ticket with repro, rollback status, and ETA for a patched rollout.

Olivia: putting follow-up reminder in case: add monitoring alert for response-coherence-regression (pattern: repeated token subsequences after truncation) so we can catch earlier instead of relying on customer reports.

Jordyn: +1, I'll add a lightweight autodetector in the nightly eval that runs with long prompts and flags repeats / early terminations.

Liam: good. assigning owners: jordyn -> bug+tests, liam -> rollout plan, olivia/tara -> customer comms. keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
